section_title: Why are the gifts weighed and placed in named hands?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 24 Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, together with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers, 25 and I weighed out to them the contribution of silver and gold and the articles that the king, his counselors, his leaders, and all the Israelites there had offered for the house of our God. 26 I weighed out into their hands 650 talents of silver, articles of silver weighing 100 talents, 100 talents of gold, 27 20 gold bowls valued at 1,000 darics, and two articles of fine polished bronze, as precious as gold.

28 Then I told them, “You are holy to the LORD, and these articles are holy. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers. 29 Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the chambers of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem before the leading priests, Levites, and heads of the Israelite families.” 30 So the priests and Levites took charge of the silver and gold and sacred articles that had been weighed out to be taken to the house of our God in Jerusalem.

context_lines: Ezra sets apart leading priests together with Sherebiah, Hashabiah and their brothers. He weighs out to them the silver, gold and articles offered for God’s house by the king, his officials and the Israelites.
He reminds them that both they and the articles are set apart to the LORD. They must guard the gifts until they can be weighed before the leaders in Jerusalem.
Trust in God is accompanied by named responsibility and a check on delivery. The gifts belong to the purpose for which they were offered, and their care can be accounted for.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezra/8.htm) connects the concern for God’s gifts with faithful care for what belongs to Him. [Gill](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/ezra/8.htm) emphasizes that the same weight is to be delivered in the presence of witnesses. The procedure protects the offering and gives the carriers a clear responsibility.
god_plan_lines: A related concern appears in [2 Corinthians 8:16–24](https://biblehub.com/bsb/2_corinthians/8.htm). Paul arranges for trusted people to accompany a generous offering and explains that care is being taken to do what is right before both God and other people.

The parallel is responsible care for gifts entrusted to ministry. In both settings, confidence in God goes together with arrangements other people can see and assess. Practical accountability serves the generosity rather than detracting from it.
